item.title: MSMS 2.6.2 released
item.description:
MSMS 2.6.2 is out for Linux 64-bit. It makes MSMS more robust:

  • Fewer crashes. Inputs that used to crash MSMS, hang it or make it write corrupt files now work. These include surfaces with more than 2 million triangles, molecules of around 100,000 atoms and more, very large and very small spheres, and more than 253 surface components with -all_components (the limit is now 65,535). Several recovery paths after numerical problems are also fixed.
  • Duplicate atoms. Two atoms with the same centre no longer stop the run. MSMS keeps one of them, prints a warning and keeps the numbering of the input file.
  • Faster -all_components. The search for buried components now runs in parallel. With 8 threads it is about twice as fast.

The output is unchanged. For inputs that 2.6.1 handled, the .vert, .face and .area files are byte-for-byte identical to those of the 2.6.1 source built with the same compiler.

The macOS and Windows downloads are still version 2.6.1.

item.title: New lab website
item.description:
The lab’s new website is at sannerlab.github.io. It brings together:

  • a page for each of our software tools, with downloads, documentation, tutorials and a gallery. These pages used to be on ccsb.scripps.edu.
  • the downloads themselves (installers, tutorial data and PDFs). They are now in the releases of sannerlab/downloads on GitHub.
  • the lab’s publications.
  • who we are: current members, alumni and funding.
